source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes)
instrument: USFS Royce polygon legal_type field
summary: By the dataset's legal_type field, 474 polygons (1,472M polygon-acres, 73.5%) are treaty_or_agreement, 76 statute (224M, 11.2%), 113 executive_order (198M, 9.9%) and 54 unknown (108M, 5.4%). Polygon acres overlap (sum 2,002M vs about 1,597M acres of union coverage on the repo's 0.1-degree grid), so these are shares of mapped polygon area, not of land.
federal_account_contrast: The map colors all 717 polygons the same way, implying a treaty basis for all; 26.5% of mapped polygon area has no treaty link at all in the source data.
map_implication: Expose legal_type as a visible style dimension (hatch or outline) and legend it; never present the Royce layer as 'land ceded by treaty'.
notes: Acreage computed by this project from polygon geometry (spherical-excess formula), not from Royce's own acreage column. legal_type is the USFS dataset's inference from which links exist (Kappler, statute, EO), not a legal finding.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes)
nations: Western Shoshone; Goshute; Eastern and Western Apache; Paiute; Uintah Ute; Pima; Maricopa; Tohono O'odham (Papago); Yuma (Quechan); Walapai; Mohave; Hopi (Moki); Cocopah; Washoe; Methow; Okanagan; Chehalis; Chinook; Cowlitz
place: Great Basin, Southwest, interior Pacific Northwest
instrument: None (Royce records no cession instrument)
summary: Sixteen Royce areas totalling about 330M polygon-acres are, in Royce's own remarks, land the United States took possession of or 'assumed title' to with no treaty, purchase or relinquishment. The largest are 688 eastern Apache (86.0M), 444 Western Shoshone (75.7M), 689 western Apache (55.9M), 432 Uintah Ute (24.9M), 558 and 562 Paiute (23.8M, 23.4M) and 687 Pima-Maricopa-Papago (10.2M).
verbatim_quote: No treaty of purchase was ever made with this tribe. The U. S. assumed title to their country
sources_cited_by_source: Royce 1899 Schedule pp. 824-922 remarks column, as quoted in royce-entry-roles.csv
federal_account_contrast: Royce himself (a federal source) says no cession happened here, yet the map shows these as cession polygons, and the dataset's legal_type labels them statute (8), executive_order (4), treaty_or_agreement (2) or unknown (2).
map_implication: Create a class 'taken with no instrument' for these 16 areas; this is the single largest correction (about 330M polygon-acres).
notes: Quote from Royce remark on 683/685 (Walapai, Yuma). 432 quote: 'taken possession of by U. S. without formal purchase'. Royce number assignment for 558 is flagged low-confidence in the crosswalk (garbled OCR).

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes)
nations: Apache; Walapai; Yuma; Mohave; Hopi; Cocopah; Pima; Maricopa; Papago
instrument: (dataset artifact) 'statute' legal_type with 1886-10-01 date
summary: The eight Southwest 'country claimed at beginning of their relations with the U.S.' areas all carry the date 1886-10-01 and legal_type 'statute' only because a federal statute link is present in the USFS data; Royce describes no statute that ceded them. Together they are about 162M polygon-acres.
verbatim_quote: Country claimed by them at beginning of their relations with the U. S.
federal_account_contrast: A user reading 'statute, 1886' would infer a congressional cession that did not occur.
map_implication: Override legal_type for 682-689 to 'no_instrument'; do not show 1886 as a cession date in the timeline.
notes: Why the USFS record has 1886-10-01 is not established here; possibly the date of a report or map compilation. Verify against USFS attribute documentation.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes)
instrument: 18 California treaties of 1851-52 (unratified)
instrument_cite: Royce Schedule pp. 780-784; atlas instrument ids TLA-U-CA-*
summary: Royce maps California almost entirely through the 18 unratified 1851-52 treaties: 35 polygons (about 88M polygon-acres) split into 'reserve' and 'cession of all other claims' plates. All 35 carry legal_type 'unknown'. No legal cession took place under these instruments.
verbatim_quote: Cede all claim to territory outside of reserved tract
federal_account_contrast: Royce's plates show California as if ceded by these treaties; the Senate rejected them in 1852.
map_implication: Render 273-310 as 'unratified-treaty area' and mark the 'reserve' polygons as promised-then-never-set-aside land.
notes: Crosswalk note already says 'no legal cession took place'; number assignment within each treaty is by row order (OCR scrambled).

source_doc: NARA Prologue 2013 (archives.gov/publications/prologue/2013/fall-winter/treaties.pdf); Wikipedia 'California Indian Reservations and Cessions'
instrument: Senate rejection of the 18 California treaties in executive session
summary: The Senate refused to ratify the 18 treaties on July 8, 1852 and filed them under an injunction of secrecy lifted January 18, 1905. NARA's Prologue attributes the rejection to objections from white Californians and commissioner irregularities. Reported reserve acreage varies by source (7.4M to 8.5M acres).
federal_account_contrast: Promised reserves of several million acres were never set apart; the land became public domain anyway.
map_implication: Add the promised 1851-52 reserves (Royce 'reserve' polygons) as a 'promised, never delivered' layer.
notes: One source gives June 28, 1852 for the rejection; one gives 1909 for the end of secrecy. 1852/1905 are the majority readings.

source_doc: Barker v. Harvey, 181 U.S. 481 (1901) (law.resource.org); United States v. Title Insurance & Trust Co., 265 U.S. 472 (1924)
instrument: California Land Claims Act, Act of Mar. 3, 1851
summary: The 1851 Act required private land claims in California to be presented to a commission within two years or be treated as abandoned. In Barker v. Harvey the Court held Mission Indians' occupancy rights forfeited because no claim was filed for them; in 1924 the Court refused to overrule Barker as a 'rule of property'.
federal_account_contrast: Indian title in California was lost by a filing deadline under a land-title statute, not by any cession.
map_implication: Tag California areas with 'title treated as abandoned under 1851 Land Claims Act'; link Barker and Title Insurance cases.
notes: Critics (ICT) note the Indians were likely never told to file; that is advocacy commentary.

source_doc: BIA press releases 1965 and 1969 (bia.gov/node/10035; bia.gov/as-ia/opa/online-press-release/doi-recommends-bill-disposition-291-m-award-ca-indians); NPS 'Five Views'
nations: Indians of California; Mission Indians; Pit River
instrument: ICC award to the Indians of California
instrument_cite: ICC Dockets 31 and 37 (consolidated; docket numbers not confirmed by fetched sources)
summary: The ICC awarded $29.1 million (appropriated 1964) for California land; Interior described it as compensation for land 'taken by the United States March 3, 1853'. Secondary sources compute about 47 cents per acre. Pit River and other groups opposed it, and many refused checks in 1972.
verbatim_quote: land taken by the United States March 3, 1853
federal_account_contrast: Federal law treats California aboriginal title as extinguished by taking (1853) plus later payment, not by cession.
map_implication: Date of taking 1853-03-03 should be shown instead of 1851-52 treaty dates; class 'taken, compensated by ICC money award'.
notes: Separate $5M 1944 Court of Claims K-344 award under 1928 Jurisdictional Act was for unfulfilled treaty benefits, not title. Offset amounts ($17M gross / $12M offsets) are unverified.

source_doc: ICT News, 'The Court of Claims ruling in California Indians K-344'; 25 U.S.C. 661
instrument: California Indians Jurisdictional Act of May 18, 1928; Indians of California v. U.S., 102 Ct. Cl. 837
summary: Under the 1928 Act the Court of Claims compensated the unfulfilled benefits of the 18 treaties (about $5M net, 1944) and expressly said it was not paying for land cession or for a taking.
federal_account_contrast: Even the federal court refused to treat the treaties as cessions.
map_implication: Cite as evidence that 273-310 are not cessions.
notes: Gross award and offset figures unverified.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes); Statutes at Large 18 Stat. 689 (dheller.org transcription)
place: Ruby Valley, Nevada; Western Shoshone country NV/CA/ID/UT/OR
instrument: Treaty of Ruby Valley, Oct. 1, 1863 (ratified with amendment 1866; proclaimed Oct. 21, 1869)
summary: The treaty defined Western Shoshone boundaries and granted passage, telegraph, stage, railroad and mining rights, but contains no land cession. Royce maps the area (444, about 75.7M polygon-acres) and says the U.S. 'took possession' without purchase. The dataset types it treaty_or_agreement because it links to Kappler.
verbatim_quote: No formal purchase of the territorial claim of these tribes or bands was made, but the U. S. took possession of the same
federal_account_contrast: The map's color implies cession; the treaty is a peace and right-of-way treaty.
map_implication: Reclassify Royce 444 (and Goshute 447) as 'never ceded, still contested'; show Ruby Valley boundary as treaty-recognized territory.

source_doc: CIDH/IACHR Report 75/02 procedural history (cidh.oas.org/annualrep/2002eng/USA.11140b.htm); DOJ OSG briefs
instrument: Shoshone Tribe v. United States, ICC Docket 326-K
summary: The ICC found Western Shoshone title to about 24.4M acres; it held California title ended in 1853 and Nevada title was lost over time by 'gradual encroachment by whites'. A stipulated valuation date of July 1, 1872 was used and about $26M was awarded (final award 1979).
federal_account_contrast: The 'taking' is a legal fiction fixed by stipulation for valuation, not a dated instrument; Western Shoshone groups say they never agreed to it.
map_implication: Store taking_date=1872-07-01 (stipulated) with basis 'ICC finding of gradual encroachment'; style as 'taken, no instrument'.
notes: Acreage reported as 24.4M (CA+NV) in one source and 24,396,403 acres in Nevada in another; check the opinion.

source_doc: United States v. Dann, 470 U.S. 39 (1985) syllabus (chanrobles.com/usa/us_supremecourt/470/39)
instrument: Indian Claims Commission Act s.22(a)
summary: The Court held that 'payment' occurred when the $26M award was certified and deposited in a Treasury trust account, barring the tribal-title defense, even though the Western Shoshone had not accepted the money. The Court relied on the government being both judgment debtor and trustee.
verbatim_quote: this certification automatically appropriated the amount of the award and deposited it for the Tribe in an interest-bearing trust account
federal_account_contrast: Extinguishment by unilateral deposit, not by consent or cession.
map_implication: Add class marker 'title extinguished by ICC payment (unaccepted)' for 444.

source_doc: UN CERD Decision 1(68), CERD/C/USA/DEC/1 (digitallibrary.un.org/record/573142)
instrument: CERD early warning and urgent action decision
summary: CERD, at its 68th session (Feb-Mar 2006), acted on Western Shoshone requests, expressed concern that their land rights were being denied and that US measures could cause irreparable harm, and noted the US had not responded. The Western Shoshone Claims Distribution Act of 2004 authorized distribution of the award (reported as about $145-160M with interest), which many councils refuse.
federal_account_contrast: International body treats the title as live; US treats it as extinguished.
map_implication: Note the CERD decision and IACHR Report 75/02 (Dann) on 444's info panel.
notes: Operative paragraphs not retrieved; read the PDF before quoting. Also IACHR Mary and Carrie Dann, Report No. 75/02, Case 11.140 (2002).

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes); United States v. Sioux Nation, 448 U.S. 371 (1980) (law.justia.com; law.resource.org)
instrument: Agreement of Sept. 26, 1876, enacted by Act of Feb. 28, 1877
summary: Royce shows 598 (7.2M polygon-acres, Black Hills portion of the 1868 Great Sioux Reservation) and 597 (21.2M, art. 16 unceded territory) as cessions. In 1980 the Supreme Court affirmed that the 1877 Act was a taking under eminent domain, with interest on $17.1M from 1877 (about $106M in 1980). The Sioux refused payment; the fund is reported at over $1B.
federal_account_contrast: The atlas crosswalk labels 598 'ceded' (status=ceded); the Supreme Court characterized it as a taking.
map_implication: Reclassify 597/598 from 'ceded by agreement' to 'taken by statute (judicially found a taking); payment refused'.
notes: The phrase 'ripe and rank case of dishonorable dealings' (from the Court of Claims, quoted in the opinion) was not confirmed in fetched excerpts; verify before quoting. Fund size figures vary ($757M 2010; $1.3B 2011 per PBS).

source_doc: City of Sherrill v. Oneida Indian Nation, 544 U.S. 197 (2005) (law.resource.org; Cornell LII)
place: Central New York (Oneida reservation of about 300,000 acres)
instrument: 1788 Treaty of Fort Schuyler (with New York); Trade and Intercourse Act 1790; later state purchases
instrument_cite: 544 U.S. 197; County of Oneida v. Oneida Indian Nation, 470 U.S. 226 (1985)
summary: Oneida II (1985) held the Oneidas had a federal common-law claim for state purchases made without federal approval. Sherrill (2005) then barred the Nation from asserting sovereignty over reacquired land on equitable grounds (laches, acquiescence, impossibility) because two centuries had passed.
federal_account_contrast: The illegality of the state purchases was accepted; relief was denied on equity, not because the land was validly ceded.
map_implication: Class 'taken by state purchase in violation of Nonintercourse Act; claim barred by laches'. Royce does not map these state purchases as federal cessions; check gap.

source_doc: Cayuga Indian Nation v. Pataki, 413 F.3d 266 (2d Cir. 2005) (secondary summaries; NARF petition appendix)
instrument: New York state treaties of 1795 and 1807
summary: New York took 64,012 acres in 1795 and 3 more in 1807 under state treaties never ratified by the federal government. The district court awarded $247,911,999.42 (damages plus interest); the Second Circuit, applying Sherrill, held laches barred the possessory claim and entered judgment for defendants.
federal_account_contrast: Federal law required federal consent; none was given; land still lost.
map_implication: Add Cayuga 1795/1807 state takings as 'taken without federal instrument'.

source_doc: CS Monitor 1980-04-17; Wikipedia 'Indian Land Claims Settlements'; Maine: An Encyclopedia
nations: Passamaquoddy; Penobscot; Houlton Band of Maliseet
place: Maine (claim about 12.5M acres, two-thirds of state)
instrument: Maine Indian Claims Settlement Act, Oct. 10, 1980
instrument_cite: Pub. L. 96-420; Joint Tribal Council of Passamaquoddy v. Morton, 528 F.2d 370 (1st Cir. 1975)
summary: The tribes claimed about 12.5M acres sold by Massachusetts and Maine without federal approval under the 1790 Act. Congress settled for $81.5M (trust funds and land acquisition) and ratified the prior transfers.
federal_account_contrast: Title was extinguished by a 1980 federal statute ratifying unlawful state transactions, not by any 18th or 19th century cession.
map_implication: Maine is a Royce gap; draw the claim area with class 'taken by state, extinguished by 1980 settlement act'.
notes: Public Law and F.2d cites from memory; verify.

source_doc: Mashpee Tribe v. New Seabury Corp., 592 F.2d 575 (1st Cir. 1979); 447 F.Supp. 940 (D. Mass. 1978)
instrument: Trade and Intercourse Act claim
summary: The first Nonintercourse Act case tried to a jury: the jury found the Mashpee were not a tribe at key dates (including 1870 and 1976), so the claim failed. The tribe was federally recognized in 2007.
federal_account_contrast: Land loss upheld by finding the plaintiffs not a 'tribe', not by any cession.
map_implication: Massachusetts is a Royce gap; note Mashpee as 'taken by town/state action, claim defeated on tribal-status grounds'.
notes: Sources differ on exact jury findings by year. 2007 recognition from memory.

source_doc: Wikipedia 'Indian Land Claims Settlements' table
instrument: Rhode Island Indian Claims Settlement Act, Sept. 30, 1978
summary: Narragansett aboriginal-title claim settled in 1978 with $3.5M listed compensation and a land base (commonly given as about 1,800 acres, unverified here); Carcieri v. Salazar (2009) later blocked trust acquisition.
federal_account_contrast: Claim area was taken by colonial and state detribalization (1880 RI 'sale'), not by federal treaty.
map_implication: Rhode Island is a Royce gap; mark 'taken by state action; 1978 settlement'.
notes: 1,800 acres, 1880 detribalization and Carcieri details are from memory, not verified this session.

source_doc: Oregon Encyclopedia 'Willamette Valley Treaty Commission' and 'Willamette Valley Treaties'; ndnhistoryresearch.com (David G. Lewis, Santiam Kalapuya/Grand Ronde)
nations: Kalapuya (Santiam, Tualatin, Yamhill etc.); Molalla; Clackamas
instrument: Six Willamette Valley Treaty Commission treaties (Champoeg, 1851)
summary: Commissioners Gaines, Skinner and Allen concluded six treaties in spring 1851 reserving parts of the valley. Settlers had already claimed the land under the Donation Land Claim Act, so Dart advised against them and the Senate let them die; sources say they were 'effectively rejected through neglect'. Bands got a ratified treaty only in 1855.
federal_account_contrast: Royce shows the Willamette as ceded in 1855 (Kalapuya treaty); settlement and title-taking had already happened from 1850.
map_implication: Show 1850-55 Willamette as 'settled under federal statute before any cession'; add the unratified 1851 reserves as promised land.
notes: Western Oregon totals vary: 24 unratified treaties (Lewis) or 18 sent by Dart.

source_doc: Oregon Encyclopedia 'Oregon Donation Land Act'; Oregon History Project 'A New Legal Landscape'; ODE 'The Demise of Indian Land'
instrument: Donation Land Claim Act, Sept. 27, 1850; Oregon Organic Act, Aug. 14, 1848
summary: The 1848 Organic Act protected Indian rights to land so long as they remained unextinguished by treaty. The 1850 Donation Act nonetheless granted free land to white settlers before any ratified cession in western Oregon; Delegate Thurston had called extinguishment of Native title the 'first prerequisite step'.
verbatim_quote: so long as such rights shall remain unextinguished by treaty between the United States and such Indians
federal_account_contrast: Federal statute disposed of land before any cession, contrary to the Organic Act savings clause.
map_implication: Overlay 1850-1855 Donation claims as 'disposed of before cession' over the later Royce cession polygons.
notes: Exact Organic Act wording to be checked against 9 Stat. 323 s.1.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes); Chinook Indian Nation site (chinooknation.org); chinookstory.org; ndnhistoryresearch.com
nations: Chinook; Clatsop; Waukikum; Chehalis; Cowlitz; Klikitat
place: Tansey Point, Clatsop Plains, OR; lower Columbia, WA
instrument: Tansey Point treaties of Aug. 1851 (Anson Dart), unratified
summary: Dart's 1851 Tansey Point treaties with the Clatsop and Chinook bands were never ratified. Royce 458 (4.9M polygon-acres, WA) is recorded as Chehalis, Chinook, Cowlitz-area country taken without any treaty; the dataset types it executive_order (date of a later reserve order).
federal_account_contrast: Executive-order coloring implies a legal transfer; Royce describes none.
map_implication: Reclassify 458 as 'taken with no instrument'; draw 1851 Tansey Point reserves as unratified-treaty promised land. Chinook Indian Nation is not federally recognized.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes)
instrument: Coast treaty of Aug. 11, 1855 (unratified)
summary: Royce 397 (3.9M polygon-acres) is the unratified 1855 Oregon coast treaty area; Royce says the U.S. treated the cession as binding anyway, and the Coast (Siletz) reservation was set apart inside it by executive order of Nov. 9, 1855.
verbatim_quote: The treaties were not ratified, but the U. S. authorities assumed that the cession was binding
federal_account_contrast: Royce openly records a cession that never legally occurred.
map_implication: Class 'unratified-treaty area treated as ceded'.

source_doc: treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes)
nations: Cheyenne; Arapaho; Crow; Blackfeet; Gros Ventre; Lakota; Assiniboine; Mandan; Hidatsa; Arikara
instrument: Fort Laramie treaty of Sept. 17, 1851
summary: Royce's Schedule calls the 1851 Fort Laramie treaty 'never ratified' (the Senate amended the annuity term and the amended text was not formally ratified by all nations). Royce 426, 517, 398 and 399 (about 101M polygon-acres) are 1851 territories later ceded by other instruments.
verbatim_quote: Treaty of Fort Laramie never ratified
federal_account_contrast: The atlas and courts (Crow Tribe 1960) treat 1851 as recognizing title; Royce calls it unratified.
map_implication: Keep 1851 territories as 'treaty-recognized (unperfected instrument)' layer, separate from later cessions.
notes: Ratification status of 1851 Fort Laramie is legally disputed; Senate amendment (50 to 10 years annuities) and assent by some signers, from memory.

source_doc: Texas State Library and Archives annexation pages (tsl.texas.gov); Texas Historical Commission marker 'Brazos Indian Reservation'; treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes)
nations: Comanche; Caddo; Anadahko; Waco; Tonkawa; Lipan Apache; Wichita and others
instrument: Joint Resolution for annexation of Texas, Mar. 1, 1845
summary: Texas kept its public lands at annexation, so the federal government never held a public domain there to acquire by cession. Texas set aside 12 leagues (53,136 acres) in 1854 for the Brazos and Clear Fork reserves, emptied them in 1859 by removal to Indian Territory, and the land reverted to the state. Only 5 Royce polygons touch Texas; on the repo grid central Texas (94-103W, 28-33N) is about 45% covered, mostly by Apache 688 (a no-instrument area).
federal_account_contrast: No federal cession framework applies to most of Texas; title passed by state action and removal.
map_implication: Render Texas as 'taken by state action, no instrument' rather than blank or ceded.
notes: 5 Stat. 797 cite from memory.

source_doc: CRS R46997 (everycrsreport.com); BLM ANCSA at 50 infographic; Tee-Hit-Ton v. United States, 348 U.S. 272 (1955) (govinfo)
instrument: Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, Dec. 18, 1971
summary: No treaties were made with Alaska Natives. Tee-Hit-Ton held unrecognized aboriginal title could be taken without Fifth Amendment compensation. ANCSA extinguished aboriginal claims over more than 360M acres for about 44-45M acres and $962.5M to Native corporations.
federal_account_contrast: Royce and the atlas show nothing for Alaska; title was extinguished by a 1971 statute, not by cession.
map_implication: Add Alaska as 'extinguished by statute (ANCSA 1971), no treaty'.
notes: 1867 Treaty of Cession art. III 'uncivilized tribes' clause not verified this session.

source_doc: Apology Resolution, Pub. L. 103-150, 107 Stat. 1510 (congress.gov); UH Richardson Native Hawaiian Law Center column (M. MacKenzie)
instrument: Newlands Joint Resolution, July 7, 1898; Apology Resolution, Nov. 23, 1993
summary: After the 1893 overthrow, the Republic of Hawaii ceded about 1.8M acres of crown, government and public lands to the US by the 1898 Newlands Resolution, without Native Hawaiian consent or compensation. Congress in 1993 found Native Hawaiians never directly relinquished their claims.
verbatim_quote: never directly relinquished their claims to their inherent sovereignty as a people or over their national lands to the United States
federal_account_contrast: The only 'cession' was by the post-overthrow Republic, which Congress itself has called illegal.
map_implication: Add Hawaii as 'never ceded, still contested' (ceded lands about 1.8M acres; state controls about 1.4M).
notes: Hawaii v. OHA, 556 U.S. 163 (2009) held the Apology Resolution created no substantive rights (from memory; not verified this session).

source_doc: United States v. Sandoval, 231 U.S. 28 (1913); Mountain States Tel. v. Pueblo of Santa Ana, 472 U.S. 237 (1985) (law.resource.org)
instrument: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo 1848; Pueblo Lands Act of June 7, 1924
summary: Pueblo land is held under Spanish grants recognized after 1848, not acquired by cession. About 3,000 non-Indian claimants (12,000 people) were inside Pueblo grant boundaries by 1924; the Pueblo Lands Act set up a board to adjudicate them, with Congress acknowledging a 'moral, if not legal, obligation' for its failure to protect the lands.
verbatim_quote: moral, if not legal, obligation to make reasonable restitution
federal_account_contrast: Losses inside Pueblo grants came by encroachment and a 1924 quiet-title process, not by treaty.
map_implication: Royce has no polygons for Pueblo grants (repo grid shows the Rio Grande box fully covered by other areas, e.g. Apache 688); overlay Pueblo grants as 'never ceded; partly lost to encroachment confirmed by 1924 Act'.
notes: Quote is from the 1924 Senate committee report as quoted in 472 U.S. 237.

source_doc: (not verified this session; general knowledge)
instrument: Gadsden Purchase treaty, Dec. 30, 1853
summary: The Gadsden boundary split O'odham country without O'odham consent; the US made no treaty with them, and Royce 687 records Papago country as taken with no purchase. An ICC award for O'odham aboriginal land followed in the 1970s.
federal_account_contrast: Purchase from Mexico is not a cession by the O'odham.
map_implication: Class 'taken with no instrument' for 687; note the international boundary.
notes: Search budget exhausted before verifying ICC docket (believed Docket 345) and award amount. Verify before use.

source_doc: Royce 1899 schedule scope (LOC catalog: 'from the organization of the Federal Government to and including 1894'); treaty-land-atlas repo: data/derived/cessions.json + cession-events.json + crosswalks/royce-entry-roles.csv (Royce 1899 Schedule OCR quotes)
nations: Wampanoag; Narragansett; Pequot; Mohegan; Lenape; Powhatan; Piscataway; Catawba; Abenaki and others
place: New England, Mid-Atlantic, Tidewater and Piedmont
instrument: (none in federal record) colonial deeds, conquest, colonial and state statutes
summary: Royce covers federal-era cessions only. On the repo's 0.1-degree grid, test boxes over New England (69-73.5W, 41.5-45N), Maryland-Delaware-New Jersey and the Virginia Piedmont have 0% Royce coverage. Overall, Royce union coverage is about 1,597M acres against about 1,894M acres of contiguous-US land, so roughly 300M acres (about 16%) of the lower 48 has no Royce polygon at all, before adding Alaska and Hawaii.
federal_account_contrast: Blank areas read as either 'no Native land' or 'already settled'; in fact title passed by colonial or state means outside the federal treaty system.
map_implication: Fill Royce gaps with a 'pre-federal colonial or state taking (no federal instrument)' class rather than leaving them blank.
notes: Coverage figures computed by this project from cession-cells.json (cells may include some water); CONUS land area 1,894M acres is a standard Census figure from memory.

source_doc: USGS pubs 70114965; LOC item 80695449; ArcGIS FeatureServer 'Indian_Land_Areas_Judicially_Established_1978' (services1.arcgis.com/fBc8EJBxQRMcHlei); ICC Final Report 1978 (nill.narf.org/documents/icc_final_report.pdf)
instrument: Map 'Indian Land Areas Judicially Established' (USGS for ICC), 1:4,000,000, Albers
summary: The 1978 ICC map shows each area where a tribe proved original occupancy before the ICC or Court of Claims. A public ArcGIS FeatureServer exists with a polygon layer (layer 5) 'Indian Land Areas Judicially Established 1978' with fields including CATNUM and Affiliatio; this contradicts the repo's G2 note that no vector dataset exists. The ICC completed 546 dockets and awarded about $818.2M; it could only award money at land value at the 'time of taking'.
federal_account_contrast: Provides a federal, judicially based alternative to Royce: where title was proven and then 'taken', often with no cession.
map_implication: Evaluate the FeatureServer for a 'judicially established aboriginal title' layer (check license, CATNUM-to-docket crosswalk); join ICC docket, taking date and award per polygon.

instrument: Executive orders and acts restoring reservation land to the public domain
summary: The crosswalk marks 16 Royce areas (about 12M polygon-acres) status=taken, e.g. 699 (8.3M, remainder of Great Sioux Reservation restored by Act of Mar. 2, 1889), 717 (1.4M, north half of Colville restored by Act of July 1, 1892) and repeated White Mountain Apache restorations by executive order 1873-1893.
federal_account_contrast: Royce sometimes calls these 'ceded portions'; they were restored to public domain unilaterally.
map_implication: Use the crosswalk's existing status=taken as a separate class 'taken by statute or EO'.
notes: Colville 1892 restoration was done without tribal consent (Royce calls it 'the ceded portion'); 699 took effect with the Sioux agreement proclaimed Feb. 10, 1890, so it is mixed.

instrument: Unratified agreements underlying executive-order reserves
summary: Several reserves were set apart by executive order under agreements Congress never ratified: 557 Judith Basin (Crow, 1874), 563 Jicarilla (1874), 609 San Juan (Southern Ute, 1878 agreement), 540a Wichita (1872 agreement). Royce 368 (7.1M) was a lease, not a cession, until 1866.
federal_account_contrast: These promised reserves were later revoked or reduced without ratified instruments.
map_implication: Show these as 'promised under unratified agreement' rather than as reservations.
